slides.headline: Pregnancy massage: what to expect
slides.sub: Comfort, positioning and a few things to mention first.

slides.title: Is it OK in pregnancy?
slides.body: For most people with an uncomplicated pregnancy, massage from a trained therapist is generally considered fine. It's worth letting your midwife, GP or obstetrician know, especially if you have any complications.

slides.title: How you'll be positioned
slides.body: From the second trimester, lying flat on your back for long periods can feel uncomfortable. Side-lying with pillows between your knees and under the bump is common, and you can change position anytime.

slides.title: What it can help with
slides.body: Many people find massage eases tight shoulders, a sore lower back and heavy, tired legs. It's a helpful way to relax and feel more comfortable, alongside staying active in ways that suit you.

slides.title: Tell your therapist about
slides.body: How many weeks along you are, any complications, swelling that's new or only on one side, recent pain, and what feels good. Pressure is always adjustable, so speak up if anything feels off.

slides.title: When to check with your care team
slides.body: Contact your midwife or doctor promptly for bleeding, sudden swelling of the face or hands, a severe headache, calf pain or swelling in one leg, or reduced baby movements.

slides.headline: Book a pregnancy massage
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists tailor positioning and pressure to each stage. If your extras cover includes remedial massage, you can claim on the spot with HICAPS.

caption:
Tight shoulders, sore back, heavy legs? Pregnancy massage can be a welcome break.

For most people with an uncomplicated pregnancy, massage from a trained therapist is generally considered fine. It's worth letting your midwife, GP or obstetrician know, especially if you have any complications.

Expect side-lying with pillows between your knees and under the bump rather than lying flat for long periods. Tell your therapist how many weeks along you are, about any new or one-sided swelling, and what pressure feels good.

Contact your midwife or doctor promptly for bleeding, sudden swelling of the face or hands, a severe headache, calf pain or reduced baby movements.
